items.title: No controlled evaluation of decision templates
items.whyItMatters: All evidence is before-after or stepped by convenience.
items.opportunity: Use the rollout for a controlled comparison with chance-set order.

items.title: Few clusters of very different sizes
items.whyItMatters: Eleven boards from 8 to 60 cases a week limit power and balance.
items.opportunity: Stratify the wave order by board size and sample a fixed number of discussions per board-month.

items.title: Mid-2027 data gap for four boards
items.whyItMatters: Missing periods can bias a stepped comparison.
items.opportunity: Schedule the affected boards away from the gap and pre-specify handling of missing periods.

items.title: Patients' understanding is not measured
items.whyItMatters: Complete minutes may not mean informed patients.
items.opportunity: Use the five-item questionnaire in four languages.

items.title: Patients with limited literacy or English
items.whyItMatters: They are most at risk of mixed messages and least able to complete questionnaires.
items.opportunity: Offer help to complete it and report results by language.

reevaluation: The gaps favour a controlled comparison built into the rollout, with stratified order and explicit handling of the data gap.
summary: Five gaps; no controlled evaluation and few clusters are high severity.
